clue.text: Turning up in Germany, I got into top saloon

indicators.note: turning the word up round makes it read the other way

parts.note: the word up, given as it is before being turned

indicators.note: something that gets into another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes inside the garment

parts.note: a blouse is a top worn by women
ich is the German word for I

explanation.surface: Someone arriving in Germany manages to get into a smart saloon car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' makes PU from UP. 'Saloon' looks like a car, but it means a bar; ICH is German for 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a bar room, and by extension a drinking establishment such as a British pub.

clue.text: Requiring medication, one gets locked in pound, guarded by sailor

indicators.note: something guarded by a sailor has him on both sides of it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: PO is a petty officer, a naval rank

indicators.note: being locked in a pound puts one piece within the other

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
an ace is the card counting as one

explanation.surface: A sick prisoner locked up in a pound under a sailor's guard needs his medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like an animal enclosure; here it is the weight abbreviation. PO is a petty officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given to a patient is a kind of medication with no active ingredient.

clue.text: Calls in drone, perhaps, getting support from a US/Russian intermediary body

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece supported by another has that piece under it, so it comes after
the calls are placed in the insect, inside its letters

parts.note: a drone is a male bee, so it is an example of one
rings means telephone calls

explanation.surface: A buzzing drone makes calls with help from a diplomatic go-between body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drone' suggests an aircraft, but it is the male insect. In a down clue 'getting support from' puts A below.
explanation.definitionFit: This stretch of sea lies between Alaska and Siberia, a body of water between the US and Russia.

clue.text: Relative visiting Hollywood sees western being produced

parts.note: visiting somewhere means being in it
Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A relative on a visit to Hollywood watches a western being filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation by marriage, such as a spouse's parent, is a relative.

clue.text: Writing about movement of bat, one circling overhead

indicators.note: about here means around, so the handwriting goes around the other letters

parts.note: a hand is a style of handwriting

indicators.note: movement of the letters of bat rearranges them

explanation.surface: An essay about how a bat moves, and one flying round over our heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement of' rearranges 'bat' to ATB. 'Circling overhead' suggests the bat in flight, but it is a strip round a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon around a hat's crown encircles it, sitting on the wearer's head.

clue.text: Couple able to cope with all sorts of ups and downs?

definitions.text: Couple able to cope with all sorts of ups and downs?

parts.words: Couple able to cope with all sorts of ups and downs?
parts.note: a mechanical coupling that lets two shafts turn at any angle to each other, read as a couple who weather every change

explanation.surface: A couple who can handle every high and low of life together.
explanation.definitionFit: This engineering coupling joins two rotating shafts while letting them move at varying angles.

clue.text: Up before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.walkthrough: 'Up before court' reads like a defendant's ordeal; 'Up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something standing upright is up, the adjective sense of being raised.

clue.text: Cut across old railway line

indicators.note: the cut is placed across the old letter, going round it

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Someone cuts across the track of a disused railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old railway line' looks like one phrase, but 'old' gives O and only 'railway line' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch track that leaves the main line and rejoins it is a type of railway line.

clue.text: 'Mess' observed in space beginning to explain the big bang, right?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the big bang was the creation of the universe
room means space

explanation.surface: Some mess is seen in space as the start of an account of the big bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like chaos, but it is the room where service people relax together.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a communal room where soldiers or sailors eat and relax, a place for leisure.

clue.text: Sort of concert piano Grieg regularly used in composition

indicators.note: letters used in a composition are put together in a new order
taking letters at regular intervals picks every other one of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A piano piece by Grieg is played at a certain kind of concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes RE from Grieg, which joins PIANO to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert held outdoors rather than in a hall is described by this adjective.

clue.text: One cold coffee is brought over, and a type of pastry

indicators.note: the coffee is brought over the other letters, covering them on both sides

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single iced coffee is served, along with a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Criss-cross strips laid over a pie make a pastry topping with that name.

clue.text: Unblemished English apples, say, turned into pulp

definitions.note: a noun phrase: fruit such as apples mashed to a soft mass

parts.note: pure means unblemished, without a flaw

explanation.surface: Perfect English apples get mashed into pulp.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit cooked and sieved to a smooth paste, as with apple sauce, is the kitchen name for this.

clue.text: Novel by Mandela, perhaps, found in shop?

parts.note: novel means new
Nelson Mandela was a South African gentleman: SA for South African plus gent

explanation.surface: A novel by Nelson Mandela turns up in a bookshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells papers and magazines is the person a customer meets behind a corner shop's counter.

clue.text: "Roughly speaking, its use is passed on from father to son", I interjected

definitions.text: Roughly speaking, its use is passed on

indicators.note: interjected means thrown in between, so this letter goes inside the others

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone quoted on how a rough way of speaking passes down a family, with an interruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly speaking' sounds like 'approximately', but it describes rough local speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A local dialect, considered unrefined, is learned and handed down through families.

clue.text: Leeds United's centre-half battles to help secure highest position in years

indicators.note: united means joined together into something new, so the letters of Leeds are rearranged
the centre of the word battles is its middle letter

explanation.surface: The Leeds United centre-half fights to help his team reach their highest place in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leeds United' suggests the football club; 'United' signals the rearranging. A centre-half is a central defender.
explanation.definitionFit: Being first-born among siblings puts a person at the top position by age.

clue.text: So, how does industrialist make it?

definitions.meaning: so as an intensifier, as in so tired, meaning very greatly
only the outer letters, the first and last, of industrialist spell the word it: the word is made at the extremes

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a tycoon achieves success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make it' looks like success, but it is the word 'it', which is the first and last letters of 'industrialist': it is made by the extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: As an intensifier, 'so' as in 'so tired' means very greatly.

clue.text: Hand around drug at a lavish party

indicators.note: the hand goes around the drug, holding it inside

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs are passed round at an extravagant party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand around' looks like a verb meaning pass round, but HAND is a noun put around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival or celebration, especially in Spanish-speaking countries, is a big party.

clue.text: Almost certain Lear's 'nonsense' is this

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: nonsense here describes the letters of Lear jumbled up

explanation.surface: Edward Lear's nonsense verse is almost certainly of this dreamlike kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote famous nonsense poems, such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre, dreamlike writing like Lear's nonsense verse is described as having this quality.

clue.text: Given time, American golfer makes a comeback — it's a struggle

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: An American golfer gets some time and stages a comeback, though it is a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American golfer' looks like one person, but American gives US and the golfer is Ernie Els.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous scuffle or fight, which is a struggle.

clue.text: Playing partners provided short term solution for anxiety?

parts.note: in bridge, South and North play as partners
if means provided, on condition that

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the word term, before it is cut

explanation.surface: Golf partners provided a short-term fix for nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S are partners at the bridge table. 'Solution' is a liquid, a small drink to steady the nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick drink of spirits is a traditional calmer for nerves, the liquid sense of solution.

clue.text: Handicap event in which number is displayed on back

parts.note: hind means at the back

indicators.note: the event holds the number within it
the number is shown inside the event's letters

parts.note: a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: A handicap race where runners wear their numbers on their backs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handicap event' looks like a kind of race, but only 'Handicap' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is an obstacle or impediment, something holding a person back.

clue.text: Be off work during strike

indicators.note: the work happens during the strike, so it goes inside it

parts.note: to hit is to strike
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone takes time off work while the strike is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like industrial action; it means to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British slang command to go away, meaning be off with you.

clue.text: Famous piece of music has depth

parts.note: a note is a small piece of music

explanation.surface: A famous piece of music has great depth.
explanation.definitionFit: A noted person is well known, which is to say renowned.

clue.text: Clubs or spades in play?

indicators.note: play here means loose movement, so the letters are moved about freely

parts.note: the words or and in taken as written, with spades giving S, its card-game abbreviation

explanation.surface: A card-game question: are clubs or spades in play?
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs and spades look like card suits; 'Clubs' is the golfer's kind, and OR, S and IN are shuffled by 'play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs with angled metal heads are called by this name, a sporting sense.

clue.text: Engine driver leaves a halt

indicators.note: when a letter leaves the word it is taken out

parts.note: steam is what drives a steam engine

explanation.surface: A train driver walks away from a small railway halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halt' looks like a little station, but it is the verb meaning to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or check it.

clue.text: Plan for aircraft carrier initially welcomed

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the aircraft welcomes a letter in, holding it inside

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word carrier

explanation.surface: A plan to build an aircraft carrier is welcomed at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aircraft carrier' looks like one ship, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or planned undertaking is a project.

clue.text: Hospital department repeatedly on strike, ultimately seeking agreement

indicators.note: repeatedly means the department's letters are written twice

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word strike

explanation.surface: A hospital department keeps striking, and wants a settlement in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, a diplomatic accord.

clue.text: One used to extract water — diviner emptied out the old glass bottles

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the glass holds the other letters

parts.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass

indicators.note: emptying a word leaves only its outer letters

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A water diviner empties old glass bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One used to extract water' sounds like a diviner's rod, but it is a laundry machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A drying machine spins wet laundry in hot air, removing moisture from it.
